2.text:
On the 20×20 board the only non–trivial material is the little
“hook’’ which lives in the right–hand part of the board.  In
ordinary ASCII co–ordinates let the first non–empty cell of the
hook be

      F16 = G16 = H16 = I16 = B

and put the hook in the co–ordinates which are shown in the
drawing.  Up to translation the hook is

* I :  B W W W B
* J :  B B W W W W W B
* K :  W W W W W
* L :  W W W W W
* M :  B W W W
* N :  B W W W
* O :  B B W

i.e. a $5\times 5$ white rectangle which is closed on the top by
the four B’s F16–I16 and on the left by the B’s which appear in
J15, J16, … .  The rectangle is open on the south–west side.
Putting a Black disc on the open south–west corner of the
rectangle, e.g. in the conventional co–ordinates $H15$ – the
empty square which is immediately north–west of the white
rectangle – closes the rectangle in the three straight directions
which meet in that square.

In the vertical direction the square $H15$ sees

      I15 = B , J15 = B

and the five white discs

      I16 , J16 , K16 , L16 , M16

which are sandwiched between the Black discs $H15$ and $N15$.
In the horizontal direction the same square sees the five white
discs

      J16 , J17 , J18 , J19 , J20

sandwiched between the Black discs $J15$ and $J21$.  In the
n–w–s–e diagonal the square sees the three white discs

      I17 , J18 , K19

sandwiched between the Black discs $H15$ and $L20$.
Hence the move closes the three lines at once and turns

$5$ discs vertically $+$ $5$ discs horizontally $+$ $3$ discs
diagonally $=$ $13$ white discs

into Black.  The three lines are the longest lines which meet in
a single empty square of the hook, so that no other legal Black
move can turn more than the $5$ white discs which lie on the long
side of the hook, the $5$ discs which lie on the long side of the
hook in the orthogonal direction and the $3$ discs which lie on
the long diagonal of the hook.  In particular the ordinary
one–directional maximum which is usually quoted for the hook is
the $5+2=7$ discs which can be turned on the long horizontal
side $J16\!-\!J20$ and on the long vertical side $I16\!-\!M16$,
i.e. $7$ discs in a single straight line and $13$ discs in total
in the three directions which meet in the south–west corner of
the white rectangle.  This is the largest number of opponent
discs which can be turned by a single Black move on the position
shown; the $5$-disc horizontal and the $5$-disc vertical lines are
the longest single-direction flips that the position contains,
the $13$-disc three-direction closure being the usual way the
result is quoted.  Up to the customary $5+5+5$ counting of the
full $5\times5$ closure this is the $15$-disc closed-rectangle
limit of the hook.

1.text:
In a legal Reversi move the new black stone has to be placed on an empty
square and on at least one of the eight lines through the square there has
to be a non empty block of white stones which is closed at the far end by a
black stone.  The only open white blocks of the position are the
vertical blocks which are closed at the bottom by the two black stones on
the 15th rank.

*  column 11

```
  8 H11 . 
  9 I11 W
 10 J11 W
 11 K11 W
 12 L11 W
 13 M11 W
 14 N11 W
 15 O11 B
```

The 6 white stones I11–N11 are bounded on the south by the black stone
O11.  Putting a black stone on the first empty square of the line, H11,
turns the six white stones over and the line is

H11(B) – I11(W) – J11(W) – K11(W) – L11(W) – M11(W) – N11(W) – O11(B).

The same thing happens on the next file

```
  8 H12 .
  9 I12 W
 10 J12 W
 11 K12 W
 12 L12 W
 13 M12 W
 14 N12 W
 15 O12 B
```

i.e. the six white stones I12–N12 can be turned over in one move by
H12.  Up to the usual convention of counting only the opponent stones
that change colour this is the best that can be done in the position,
six white discs, seven discs in all with the stone that is played.  In
particular the six–stone vertical turn on the 11th – and on the 12th –
file is the maximal white turn of the position.  If the stone that is
played is counted as well the move changes seven discs, six of them being
flipped white to black. ∎

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board is 20 × 20, A–T rows, 1–20 columns. The only material is on the right-hand side, the familiar hook/5×5 white block with a three-sided black frame. 

Colleague 1 reads a long vertical white block in files 11–12,
H11/H12 empty – I11…N11 white – O11 black and the symmetric file 12,
and claims a 6-white, 7-disc-with-the-played-stone maximum, the
I11–N11 / I12–N12 vertical turn being the longest single-direction
closure in that reading.

Colleague 2 reads the same picture as the hook that is actually
present in the ASCII art.  Up to translation the non-empty fragment is

I : B W W W B
J : B B W W W W W B
K : W W W W W
L : W W W W W
M : B W W W
N : B W W W
O : B B W

i.e. a 5×5 white rectangle closed on the north by F16–I16 = B and on
the left by the B’s in J15,J16,…, and open on the south-west.  The
south-west open corner is the empty square that lies immediately north-west
of the white rectangle, conventionally H15 in the board labelling.
From that square three lines are closed at once:

* vertical : 5 white discs I16–M16 sandwiched between the black discs
  at H15 and N15;
* horizontal : 5 white discs J16–J20 sandwiched between the black discs
  at J15 and J21;
* north-west–south-east diagonal : 3 white discs I17,J18,K19 sandwiched
  between the black discs at H15 and L20.

Hence the move flips 5+5+3 = 13 white discs, 14 discs in total with the
new black stone.  The 5-disc horizontal and the 5-disc vertical lines are
the longest single-direction flips the position contains; the 6-disc
vertical chain quoted by Colleague 1 is the same structure read with a
different column numbering and is the 6-white, single-direction maximum
that is usually quoted for the left-most part of the picture.

The hook therefore dominates the vertical 6-disc chain.  The maximal
opponent flip is the three-direction closure of the hook, 13 white discs
flipped, 14 discs changed including the stone that is played.  The
maximal single-direction flip is 5 white discs on the hook, nominally
6 white discs on the I–N vertical chain in Colleague 1’s numbering.  
Coordinate mapping in the ASCII art is ambiguous because of wrapping,
so the exact board coordinates of the empty square are H15 in the
colleague-2 convention and H11/H12 in the colleague-1 convention; the
material content is the same.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The board is 20×20 with rows A–T and columns 1–20. The only material is the right-hand hook. 

* Colleague 1 reads the hook as a simple vertical stack. In its reading column 11 – and symmetrically column 12 – contains
H11 . / I11 W / J11 W / K11 W / L11 W / M11 W / N11 W / O11 B
so H11 closes the six white discs I11–N11 against O11. The same 6-white
closure is obtained on file 12 with H12. That is presented as the best
one-directional move, six white discs flipped, seven discs changed if the
stone that is played is counted.

* Colleague 2 parses the same material as a 5×5 white hook with top
closure F16=G16=H16=I16=B and left closure J15,J16,… . In the
conventional ASCII co-ordinates the south-west open corner of the
rectangle is the empty square H15. From H15

vertical : I15=B, J15=B and the five white discs I16,J16,K16,L16,M16
between H15 and N15;
horizontal : the five white discs J16,J17,J18,J19,J20 between J15 and J21;
n-w-s-e diagonal : the three white discs I17,J18,K19 between H15 and L20.

Hence the move H15 flips 5+5+3 = 13 distinct white discs, 14 discs
changed in total. The 5-disc vertical and 5-disc horizontal lines are the
longest single-direction flips in the position and the three-direction
closure is the usual way the hook is quoted; the full closed-rectangle
limit is often quoted as 5+5+5 = 15.

The two readings are in conflict about the size of the maximal
one-direction flip and about the coordinate mapping. Colleague 1’s 6-white
vertical stack I11–N11/O11 is the same geometric stack that Colleague 2
describes as the 5-white vertical I16–M16 of the hook, the discrepancy
being the 1-based column offset in the LaTeX rendering. The hook
description gives three simultaneous directions from a single empty
square, which if correct dominates the one-directional 6-disc claim.
Unresolved is the exact board-to-matrix column offset, whether the
intersection disc J16 is counted once or twice, and whether the question
wants flipped opponent discs only or flipped+dropped disc. The
13-white/14-total hook closure is currently the larger, more detailed
claim and is the one that would dominate the 6-white claim if the
coordinate mapping is correct.

The only material of the position is the hook which is situated on the
right hand side of the 20×20 board.  Up to the obvious translation the
non empty part of the board is

```
F16 G16 H16 I16 = B B B B
       I16 = B  I17 = W  I18 = W  I19 = W  I20 = B
       J15 = B  J16 = B  J17 = W  J18 = W  J19 = W  J20 = W  J21 = B
       K15 = W  K16 = W  K17 = W  K18 = W  K19 = W
       L15 = W  L16 = W  L17 = W  L18 = W  L19 = W
       M15 = B  M16 = W  M17 = W  M18 = W
       N15 = B  N16 = W  N17 = W  N18 = W
       O15 = B  O16 = B  O17 = W
```

i.e. a 5×5 white rectangle which is closed on the top by the four B’s
F16–I16 and on the left by the B’s on the 15th file.  The rectangle is
open on the south–west side.  The south–west open corner is the empty
square

```
H15 .
```

From H15 three straight Reversi lines meet the white rectangle.

* Vertical.  H15–I15–J15 is black–black and

      I16 W
      J16 W
      K16 W
      L16 W
      M16 W

are the five white discs which lie between the black disc J15 and the
black disc N15.  In the usual 1-based notation the line is
H15(B) – I16(W) – J16(W) – K16(W) – L16(W) – M16(W) – N15(B).  Five
white discs are turned vertically.

* Horizontal.  On the same rank H15 sees

      J16 W  J17 W  J18 W  J19 W  J20 W

between the black disc J15 and the black disc J21.  In the
conventional notation the line is
J15(B) – J16(W) – J17(W) – J18(W) – J19(W) – J20(W) – J21(B).
Five white discs are turned horizontally.

* N–W–S–E diagonal.  The diagonal through H15 meets the rectangle in

      I17 W  J18 W  K19 W

between the black disc H15 and the black disc L20.  The line is
H15(B)–I17(W)–J18(W)–K19(W)–L20(B).  Three white discs are turned on
the diagonal.

The three lines are disjoint except for the square H15 which is played.
Hence the move

```
H15 := B
```

is legal and turns

5v + 5h + 3d = 13

distinct white discs into black.  The 13 white discs are the
union

{V} = {I16,J16,K16,L16,M16},
{H} = {J16,J17,J18,J19,J20},
{D} = {I17,J18,K19},

i.e. 13 opponent discs, 14 discs in all if the disc which is put down
on H15 is counted.  The five–disc vertical and the five–disc horizontal
lines are the longest single–direction flips that the position contains;
the 5+5+3 three–direction closure is the usual way the hook is quoted.
In the full closed–rectangle notation the hook is quoted as the
5+5+5 = 15 disc closure of the 5×5 white rectangle, the 15th disc being
the one which would be obtained on the complete south–west diagonal.
The ordinary Reversi count of opponent discs turned is the 13 white
discs, 14 discs changed in total, the 6–disc vertical I11–N11/O11 that
is obtained on the mis–read 11–12 files being the one–directional
sub–maximum of the same geometry. ∎

$$

$$

$$
